record.paper_title: Open Problems in Constructive Function Theory
record.original_question: Let S^{q-1} be the unit sphere in Euclidean space, with surface measure. For a finite set of nodes B on the sphere, when does there exist an interpolatory positive quadrature formula based on B that is exact for spherical polynomials of the highest possible degree? In particular, if B is extremal for some energy problem, must such an interpolatory quadrature formula exist, and conversely, if an interpolatory quadrature formula exists, must B arise as the extremal set for some discretized energy problem?

evidence.quote: The questions are: (1) If B is an extremal system of points with respect to some energy problem, does there exists an interpolatory quadrature formula based at these points? (2) If an interpolatory quadrature formula exists, then is it necessarily based on the extremal points for some discretized energy problem?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S^{q-1} \subset \mathbb{R}^q$ denote the unit sphere, equipped with its normalized surface measure $\sigma$. For an integer $n \geq 0$, let $\mathcal{P}_n$ be the space of spherical polynomials of degree at most $n$ restricted to $S^{q-1}$, and set $d_n = \dim \mathcal{P}_n$. Given a finite set of nodes $B = \{x_1, \ldots, x_N\} \subset S^{q-1}$, an interpolatory quadrature formula based on $B$ for $\mathcal{P}_n$ is a set of real weights $w_1, \ldots, w_N$ such that
$$\int_{S^{q-1}} p(x)\, d\sigma(x) = \sum_{j=1}^N w_j\, p(x_j) \quad \text{for all } p \in \mathcal{P}_n,$$
where $n$ is chosen as large as possible (typically requiring $N = d_n$). The quadrature is called positive if $w_j > 0$ for all $j$. A node set $B \subset S^{q-1}$ with $|B| = d_n$ is called extremal with respect to an energy functional $E$ (for example a discretized logarithmic or Riesz energy, or a Fekete-type determinant maximization on $\mathcal{P}_n$) if it optimizes $E$ over all $d_n$-point configurations on $S^{q-1}$.

Address the following two questions:

(1) If $B$ is an extremal configuration with respect to some energy problem of the above type, must there exist an interpolatory positive quadrature formula on $B$ that is exact for $\mathcal{P}_n$?

(2) Conversely, if a finite set $B \subset S^{q-1}$ admits an interpolatory positive quadrature formula exact for $\mathcal{P}_n$ with $|B| = d_n$, must $B$ coincide with the extremal configuration for some discretized energy problem?
artifact.category_tag: Spherical quadrature and extremal point systems
artifact.status_search_result: Work by Sloan and Womersley (and subsequent authors) shows numerically and in special cases that extremal (maximum-determinant / Fekete) point systems on $S^2$ yield interpolatory cubature rules with positive weights, at least up to degree 191. However, a general proof that extremal systems always produce positive interpolatory quadratures, and the converse characterization, do not appear to have been established. The questions as stated remain open.

status_evidence.title: Extremal Systems of Points and Numerical Integration on the Sphere
status_evidence.snippet: Extremal systems for S² of degrees up to 191 are found numerically to yield interpolatory cubature rules with positive weights.
status_evidence.claim: Numerical evidence supports a positive answer to (1) on S^2 up to moderate degree but no general proof is given.

status_evidence.title: Extremal points on the sphere (Sloan-Womersley)
status_evidence.snippet: Extremal fundamental systems have surprisingly good integration properties if used to determine an interpolatory integration rule.
status_evidence.claim: The connection between extremality and positive interpolatory quadrature remains an empirical/conjectural observation.
